newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Importer pushes Bulgaria lev to record low close.
newsitem.headline: Importer pushes Bulgaria lev to record low close.

text.p: Bulgaria's currency lost 10 levs to the dollar, closing at a record low 269-270 on the interbank market on a fuel importers' dollar demand.
"A large fuel importer was bidding for dollars amid very low supply, and this was the main reason for the lev slump," a commercial bank dealer said.
The trader declined to identify the company.
Another dealer said demand for volumes as light as $100,000 instantly pushed interbank dollar asks by one lev.
The central bank tried to slow down the fall, selling dollars from 262.50 levs in the morning to 268 in the afternoon, dealers said. Central bank officials declined comment.
The lev came under rising pressure also due to a dollar rush on the cash market where dollars were sold between 266-268 in the morning and 272-275 levs in the afternoon, traders said.
"People have become quite bullish on the dollar and try to convert lev savings in hard currency after the dollar accelerated its advance (against the lev) this week," the second dealer said.
The lev ended down from 260 per dollar at the previous close and 266-267.50 this morning, dealers said.

The lev traded between 252-254 per dollar on Monday after easing from 239 to 248 in the past two weeks. It traded near 70 per dollar at the beginning of the year. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
